question.text: Ganga Growth Fund (Cat II) projects FCF of INR 120 crore in Year 5 for its portfolio company Kaveri Foods. Expected perpetual growth rate = 4%, WACC = 12%. What is the terminal value at end of Year 5?

explanation.text: The Logic: Terminal Value (Gordon growth) = FCF(T+1) / (WACC - g) = [120 x 1.04] / (0.12 - 0.04) = 124.8 / 0.08 = INR 1,560 crore. FCF must be grown by (1 + g) before division by (WACC - g). The Trap: INR 1,500 crore uses Year 5 FCF directly (120/0.08) without growing it by (1 + g); INR 1,000 crore uses the WACC without subtracting g; INR 1,250 crore mixes up the growth and discount inputs. Note: The workbook supports terminal value computed as FCF(T+1)/(WACC - g) and acknowledges that higher terminal growth assumptions may be justified in high-growth or sunrise industries.
